newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AGL says Botany plant may proceed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AGL says Botany plant may proceed.

text.p: The Australian Gas Light Company (AGL) said on Thursday it had been advised by ALISE Energy Australia Pty Ltd that a proposed cogeneration plant at Botany in Sydney may now proceed in two stages.

Under a two-stage project, the initial stage would require the supply of about 12 petajoules of gas a year, compared with initial estimates for the whole project of more than 20 petajoules a year, AGL said in a statement.
The timing of the second stage would depend on satisfactory growth in the electricity market.
AGL announced last October it had reached agreement with Santos and ALISE Energy for the supply of gas to the proposed Botany cogeneration power plant.

The proposed plant would generate electricity from natural gas from South Australia's Cooper Basin However, a Gas Heads of Agreement expired on January 31, 1997 as arrangements for the sale of electricity from the project had not been finalised.
AGL said it was continuing negotiations with Santos and ALISE with the aim of finalising an agreement.
The involvement of other South Australian Cooper Basin Producers would also be required for the project to proceed.
ALISE Energy Australia is a consortium consisting of Air Liquide, Energy Australia (the former Sydney Electricity), and Itochu Corp of Japan.
Other Cooper Basin producers include Exxon Corp's Delhi Petroleum unit, Boral Ltd and Crusader Ltd CSD.AX.
